q: What is the default domain name format every new Microsoft Entra tenant receives?
exp: Every new tenant gets an initial domain in the form <name>.onmicrosoft.com, which you can't remove. You add custom domains such as contoso.com on top and verify them with a DNS record. azurewebsites.net and cloudapp.net are used by App Service and cloud services, not Entra ID.

q: You add contoso.com as a custom domain. Which DNS record do you create at the registrar to verify ownership?
opts: A TXT (or MX) record with the value Entra provides
An A record pointing to Entra ID
exp: To prove you own contoso.com, Entra ID gives you a unique value to publish in DNS as a TXT record (an MX record also works). Entra ID looks the record up and marks the domain as verified. A, CNAME and SRV records point to services; they don't prove ownership in this process.

q: Which user attribute is the actual sign-in name of a Microsoft Entra user?
exp: The userPrincipalName (UPN), in the form name@domain, is what the user types to sign in. displayName is only the friendly name shown in lists, mailNickname is the email alias, and employeeId is an HR attribute. Changing the display name never changes how the user signs in.

q: Which PowerShell module is the current Microsoft-recommended way to manage Entra users from scripts?
exp: The AzureAD and MSOnline modules are retired. Microsoft Graph PowerShell (the Microsoft.Graph module, with cmdlets such as New-MgUser and Update-MgUser) is the supported replacement. Az.Accounts handles Azure sign-in, not Entra user management.

q: Which Azure CLI command creates a new Entra user?
exp: Entra ID objects are managed under az ad. az ad user create needs at least --display-name, --user-principal-name and --password. az user, az entra and az account user are not valid command groups for creating users.

q: A user was permanently deleted 45 days ago. What can you do to recover the account?
opts: Restore from the Deleted users blade
Nothing — after 30 days the user is permanently deleted; create a new account
Open a support ticket to restore it with the same object ID
exp: Deleted users stay in Deleted users for 30 days, during which you can restore them with everything intact. After 30 days they're permanently deleted and can't be recovered — not even by support. You'd have to create a new account.

q: Users are synchronized from on-premises Active Directory with Entra Connect. Where must you change a synced user's job title?
opts: In on-premises Active Directory (the source of authority)
exp: For users synced from on-premises AD with Entra Connect, on-premises AD is the source of authority. Change attributes such as job title there, and the change syncs to Entra ID. Edits made in the Entra admin center would be blocked or overwritten.

q: Which TWO actions can a standard member user perform by default in a new tenant?
opts: Create Azure subscriptions in the tenant without billing
exp: By default, member users can register applications and invite guests; admins can turn both off in user settings and external collaboration settings. Members can't assign Entra admin roles, and creating subscriptions needs a billing account or offer.

q: You need to block a user from signing in immediately without deleting the account. What do you do?
exp: Setting 'Account enabled' to No (blocking sign-in) stops the user from authenticating straight away, while keeping the account, its group memberships, licences and data. Removing licences or groups doesn't stop sign-in, and changing the display name has no effect on access.

q: Which Entra built-in role is the least-privileged role that can create users, reset passwords for non-admins, and manage groups?
exp: User Administrator manages users and groups and can reset non-admin passwords. Helpdesk Administrator can only reset passwords for limited roles; it cannot create users.

q: A helpdesk team must reset passwords for non-administrator users only. Least-privilege Entra role?
exp: Password Administrator and Helpdesk Administrator can reset passwords for non-administrators (and some limited admin roles), which is all a helpdesk needs. User Administrator can also create and manage users, Global Administrator can do everything, and Privileged Authentication Administrator can reset any user, including admins.

q: Where do you restrict which external domains your users may invite guests from?
opts: External collaboration settings (allow/deny list of domains)
exp: External collaboration settings include collaboration restrictions, where you can allow invitations only to specific domains (allow list) or block specific domains (deny list). Conditional Access and named locations control sign-in conditions, and Azure Policy controls resources.

q: You want only admins and users in the Guest Inviter role to be able to invite guests. Where is this configured?
opts: External collaboration settings → Guest invite settings
exp: Guest invite settings, under External collaboration settings, control who can invite guests: anyone, member users, only users in admin roles and the Guest Inviter role, or nobody. App registrations, password reset and device settings don't control invitations.

q: What does a guest receive when invited through B2B collaboration?
opts: An invitation email with a redemption link
A new mailbox in your tenant
Nothing — access is instant without any action
exp: B2B guests get an invitation email (or a direct link) and redeem it by signing in with their own account and consenting to your tenant's permissions. You never send them a password, they don't get a mailbox in your tenant, and until they redeem, their status shows as pending.

q: You must invite 300 partner users at once. Which approach takes the least effort in the portal?
opts: Bulk invite using a CSV file in the Users blade
Create them as members with new passwords
exp: Users → Bulk operations → Bulk invite takes a CSV file with each guest's email address and an optional message, and sends all the B2B invitations at once. Creating member accounts with passwords would give external people internal accounts, which defeats B2B, and Azure Policy doesn't manage users.

q: Answer Yes or No to each statement about B2B guests:
stmts: A guest can be added to a security group
A guest can be assigned an Azure RBAC role on a resource group
A guest must have an Entra ID P2 license to be invited
Guest invitation status can be 'Pending acceptance'
exp: Guests can be added to security groups and given Azure RBAC roles, just like members. Inviting guests doesn't need a P2 licence. Until a guest redeems their invitation, their status shows as 'Pending acceptance'.

q: By default, how much can guests see in your directory compared to members?
opts: Restricted — they can see limited properties of users and groups they belong to
Nothing at all, not even their own profile
exp: By default, guests have limited directory access: they can see their own profile and limited details of other users and of groups they belong to, but they can't browse the whole directory like members. You can make guest access more or less restrictive in External collaboration settings.

q: Which group type gives members a shared mailbox, calendar, and SharePoint site?
exp: A Microsoft 365 group gives its members shared collaboration tools: a mailbox, calendar, SharePoint site, Planner and Teams integration. A security group is only for access and policies, and a distribution list only sends email.

q: You need a group whose members are all Windows 11 devices, to target a device configuration. Which TWO choices together are required?
exp: Devices can only be members of security groups, and dynamic device membership adds every device that matches a rule, such as Windows 11 (deviceOSType and deviceOSVersion). Microsoft 365 groups can't contain devices, and a dynamic user rule would add users, not devices.

q: Which rule correctly selects users whose department is Sales AND whose country is Pakistan?
exp: Dynamic membership rules use the syntax (user.property -operator "value"), with -eq for an exact match and -and / -or to combine conditions. The rule must match Sales AND Pakistan, so -and is needed; the -or option would also include every user in Pakistan. Operators such as =, == and && aren't valid in rules.

q: You change a group with 40 manually added members from Assigned to Dynamic user membership. What happens to those members?
opts: They stay forever as static members
Membership is recalculated from the rule; members who don't match the rule are removed
The change is blocked while the group has members
exp: Once a group uses dynamic membership, the rule is the only source of members. Entra ID recalculates membership from the rule, so manually added members who don't match are removed. The change isn't blocked, and nobody is converted to a guest.

q: An owner of a dynamic security group tries to manually add a user. What happens?
opts: Manual adds are not allowed — membership comes only from the rule
The user is added for 24 hours
exp: In a dynamic group, the rule decides membership, so even owners can't add or remove members manually. To include the user, change the rule or the user's attributes (such as department) so they match.

q: Who can be an owner of a Microsoft Entra security group?
exp: Group owners can be users or service principals (applications). An owner can manage the group's members and settings. Groups and devices can't be owners, and you don't need to be a Global Administrator to own a group.

q: You want users to create Microsoft 365 groups only if they belong to the group 'GroupCreators'. How is this done?
opts: A group creation restriction setting (Graph/PowerShell directory setting) allowing only that group
Assign Groups Administrator role to everyone else
exp: Microsoft 365 group creation can be restricted to members of a specified security group using the directory setting EnableGroupCreation / GroupCreationAllowedGroupId.

q: You need Microsoft 365 groups to be deleted automatically if nobody renews them after 180 days. What do you configure?
exp: A group expiration policy gives Microsoft 365 groups a lifetime, such as 180 days. Owners get renewal emails, and groups nobody renews are deleted (and can be restored for 30 days). Active groups are renewed automatically. Naming policies control names, and access reviews check membership.

q: A deleted Microsoft 365 group can be restored for how long?
exp: Deleted Microsoft 365 groups are soft-deleted for 30 days, during which you can restore them with their mailbox, files and members. After 30 days they are permanently removed. (Security groups are not soft-deleted — they're deleted immediately.)

q: Answer Yes or No to each statement:
stmts: A security group can contain another security group
A Microsoft 365 group can contain a device
A dynamic group requires Entra ID P1 for its members
exp: Security groups can contain other security groups (nesting). Microsoft 365 groups only hold users, not devices. Dynamic membership is processed in the background and can take minutes or longer. Dynamic groups need Entra ID P1 for the users in them.

q: Which statement about nested groups is correct?
opts: Group-based licensing applies to all nested members
Nested group members do NOT receive licenses assigned to the parent group
Dynamic groups can include other groups as members via rules by default
exp: Group-based licensing only applies to direct members of the group. Members of a nested group don't get the licence from the parent group. Dynamic membership rules match user or device attributes, not other groups, and nesting is supported for security groups.

q: Which Azure CLI command adds a user to a group?
opts: az ad group member add --group G1 --member-id <objectId>
exp: az ad group member add adds a member to an Entra group, using --group (name or ID) and --member-id (the object ID of the user, group or service principal). az group commands manage Azure resource groups, not Entra groups, and az role assignment create grants Azure roles rather than group membership.

q: Before you can assign a license to a user, which property must be set?
exp: A user must have usageLocation (a two-letter country code) set before you can assign a licence, because some services aren't available in every country. Job title, department and manager are optional and don't affect licensing.

q: You have 100 P1 licenses and assign them to a group with 110 members. What happens?
opts: 100 are licensed; 10 show an error for insufficient licenses
exp: Group-based licensing assigns licences only while they are available. The first 100 members get P1; the other 10 show a licence error ('not enough licences') in the group's licence view. Azure never buys licences automatically, and the shortage doesn't stop the other 100 from being licensed.

q: A user has the same license both directly assigned and inherited from a group. You remove them from the group. What happens?
opts: The license stays because of the direct assignment
The user gets two licenses until removed
exp: A user can have the same licence both directly and through a group, and the two assignments are tracked separately. Removing the group membership only removes the inherited assignment; the direct one keeps the licence active. The user isn't deleted and doesn't use two licences.

q: You assign Microsoft 365 E3 to a group but need to disable the Exchange Online service plan for that group only. How?
opts: Edit the group's license assignment and turn off the specific service plan
exp: When you assign a product such as Microsoft 365 E3 to a group, you can switch off individual service plans inside it (for example Exchange Online) for that group only. Members get the rest of the product. Conditional Access controls sign-in, not licences, and removing Exchange for the whole tenant would affect everyone.

q: Which edition comes included with any Azure subscription at no extra cost?
exp: Every Azure, Microsoft 365 and Dynamics 365 subscription includes Microsoft Entra ID Free: users, groups, basic SSO and security defaults. P1, P2 and Entra ID Governance are paid add-ons with features such as Conditional Access, PIM and access reviews.

q: Which feature requires Entra ID P2?
opts: Self-service password reset for cloud users
exp: Access reviews — regular checks of who still needs group membership, app access or roles — need Microsoft Entra ID P2 (or ID Governance), like PIM and Identity Protection. SSPR for cloud users is included in all tiers, and group-based licensing and Conditional Access need P1.

q: You must require MFA only when Identity Protection detects a risky sign-in. Which license is needed?
opts: No license — security defaults do it
exp: Risk-based Conditional Access ('require MFA when sign-in risk is medium or high') relies on Microsoft Entra ID Protection, which is a P2 feature. P1 gives ordinary Conditional Access without risk signals. Security defaults turn on MFA for everyone but can't react to risk, and Free doesn't include Identity Protection.

q: For SSPR, how many authentication methods can an administrator require a user to provide before reset?
exp: In Password reset → Authentication methods, 'Number of methods required to reset' can be set to 1 or 2. Two methods is more secure. Higher numbers aren't offered, and it isn't fixed at 1.

q: Which SSPR method is NEVER allowed for administrator accounts?
exp: Administrators always get a strong reset policy: they must use two methods, and security questions are never allowed for admin accounts because answers are easy to guess or research. App notification, email and phone (SMS) remain available to admins.

q: SSPR is set to 'Selected'. How many groups can you choose?
opts: One group (which may contain nested groups)
exp: With the Selected option you can choose exactly one group in the portal. To include more people, add them to that group or nest other groups inside it. There's no 10-group option, and the group doesn't have to be dynamic.

q: You want users to register SSPR methods the next time they sign in. Which setting?
opts: Require users to register when signing in = Yes
Notify users on password resets = Yes
exp: Password reset → Registration → 'Require users to register when signing in' = Yes prompts users to register their reset methods the next time they sign in. The notification settings only send emails after resets, and the 'number of methods required' setting controls the reset itself, not registration.

q: By default, after how many days are users asked to reconfirm their SSPR authentication information?
exp: Users are asked to reconfirm their registered SSPR methods every 180 days by default, so phone numbers and emails stay up to date. The interval can be changed (0–730 days), but 180 is the default.

q: Hybrid users reset their passwords in the cloud, but the new passwords don't work on domain-joined PCs. Writeback is enabled in Entra Connect. What else must be checked?
opts: Write back passwords to your on-premises directory is enabled under Password reset → On-premises integration
exp: Password writeback must be turned on in two places: in Entra Connect, and in the Entra admin center under Password reset → On-premises integration ('Write back passwords to your on-premises directory'). P1 is enough, and Conditional Access and security questions don't affect writeback.

q: What URL do users visit to reset a forgotten password with SSPR?
exp: Users reset forgotten passwords at https://aka.ms/sspr, which redirects to passwordreset.microsoftonline.com, or with the 'Forgot my password' link on the sign-in page. The Azure portal, My Apps and login.windows.net addresses aren't the reset portal.

q: Answer Yes or No to each SSPR statement:
stmts: SSPR registration can be combined with MFA registration
The number of methods required can exceed the number of methods enabled
You can notify all admins when another admin resets their password
SSPR for cloud-only users requires Entra ID P2
exp: Combined registration covers MFA and SSPR; required methods can't exceed enabled ones; admin notifications are available; cloud-only SSPR needs Entra ID P1 or a qualifying Microsoft 365 business plan, not P2 (Free only lets users change a known password).

q: Corporate Windows laptops that are joined to on-premises AD must also be registered in Entra ID for Conditional Access. Which join type?
exp: Microsoft Entra hybrid join is for corporate devices that are joined to on-premises Active Directory and also registered in Entra ID. That lets Conditional Access trust them. Entra join is for cloud-only corporate devices, and Entra registered is for personal (BYOD) devices.

q: You want to limit the maximum number of devices each user can join or register. Where is this set?
exp: Entra ID → Devices → Device settings has 'Maximum number of devices per user', which limits how many devices one user can join or register. Conditional Access controls sign-in conditions, Azure Policy governs Azure resources, and Intune isn't required for this limit.

q: Only members of the group 'IT-Staff' should be able to join devices to Microsoft Entra ID. Where do you configure this?
opts: Device settings → Users may join devices to Microsoft Entra = Selected
exp: Entra ID → Devices → Device settings → 'Users may join devices to Microsoft Entra' can be All, Selected or None. Choosing Selected and adding the IT-Staff group means only those users can join devices. App registrations, Conditional Access platforms and Azure RBAC roles don't control device join.

q: Which device join type supports personal iOS and Android phones?
exp: Microsoft Entra registered is designed for personal devices (BYOD) and supports Windows, macOS, iOS and Android. Entra joined and hybrid joined are for organisation-owned Windows devices (and some macOS), and domain join is an on-premises AD concept.

q: Regional helpdesk staff must reset passwords only for users in the Lahore office. What do you use?
opts: An administrative unit containing Lahore users, with Helpdesk Administrator scoped to it
exp: An administrative unit groups a subset of users (here, the Lahore office). Assigning Helpdesk Administrator scoped to that unit lets staff reset passwords only for those users. Management groups and resource groups organise Azure resources, not Entra users, and device groups don't limit admin roles.

q: Which license is required to create Conditional Access policies?
exp: Conditional Access is included from Microsoft Entra ID P1. P2 adds risk-based conditions on top (via Identity Protection), but basic Conditional Access doesn't need P2. Free doesn't include Conditional Access; it only offers security defaults.
